kurz: The grey-green ring forms when eggs cook too long: sulphur from the white combines with iron from the yolk. Harmless, but avoidable.
bild_im_kopf: Like a silver spoon tarnishing in an egg: the same sulphur stains the yolk here.
faustregeln: For a yellow yolk: cook just long enough and go straight into iced water, because otherwise the heat keeps working.
The ring is harmless; it only makes the taste a little sulphurous.

ursachen.warum: With long heating the white releases hydrogen sulphide. It moves to the yolk and forms grey-green iron sulphide with its iron.
fix: Boil hard-boiled eggs for about 10 to 11 minutes, no longer

ursachen.warum: In hot water or in the air the reaction continues even after the hob is off.
fix: Put them straight into iced water

ursachen.warum: With age the egg white becomes more alkaline. Hydrogen sulphide then forms more easily.
fix: Keep the cooking time on the short side for older eggs

q1.frage: Did the eggs boil for no more than about 11 minutes?

q2.frage: Did they then sit in the warm water for a while?
